components.title: Custard
steps: Slice day-old challah bread into thick pieces and let sit to dry out.
Heat heavy cream and whole milk on low until around 135°F (warm), stirring frequently to prevent burning on the bottom.
Whisk egg yolks with sugar, cinnamon, and sea salt.
Once dairy is heated, slowly pour a little of the warm dairy into the yolk mixture while whisking to temper the eggs and prevent them from cooking.
Continue pouring in the remaining dairy until all is mixed to form a custard.
Let the custard cool a little while staying lukewarm.

components.title: Cooking and Serving
steps: Heat a pan on mid-low and melt some butter.
Dunk the bread in the custard for 15 seconds per side.
Gently cook over mid-low to low heat until brown, then flip.
Keep the cooked French toast under a towel to stay hot.
Serve with warm Vermont maple syrup, cinnamon and sugar, berries, and powdered sugar as desired.

yield.evidence: Uses 4 egg yolks, 1 cup cream, 2 cups milk, and a loaf of challah, which typically yields about 4 servings of thick-cut French toast.
